pairs.why: A's background stays a bright yellow-orange with only mild darkening at the edges, like the real cards' high-key stripes, while B's deeper orange sides and corners add a vignette the real cards lack.

A keeps a darker red body against the bright sand and sky, close to the real cooler's clear value split, while B's whiter lid and brighter body flatten the hero-to-background contrast; the margin is small.
A has a lighter, softer overall key and a gentle cast shadow, while B has darker orange top corners and a heavy dark shadow, which the real cards don't show.
B's tones are calmer, with fewer hard specular highlights on the locker, though its smaller hero and flatter interior leave it only slightly ahead.
A has a lighter, softer green wall with a pale glow behind the unit, like the real card's high-key low-contrast field, while B's wall is darker with stronger stripe contrast.
A's muted dusk sky and sand give the soft, mid-key, low-contrast look of the real pump card, while B's saturated, darker rocks and barrel and brighter sun push the contrast harder.

A's hero and truss are dark navy against a mid-value cyan-to-deep-blue background that darkens at the bottom, like the real card, while B's lighter blue body and pale grey truss weaken that dark-hero separation.
Both rovers have the same dark grey ground, white body and black wheel masses, so value and contrast give no reason to prefer either.
